job.title: u21 Head Coach
job.html_description:
The U21 Head Coach plays a pivotal role in delivering the Academy's player development strategy, creating a high performance environment that prepares young players for the demands of professional football. Responsible for leading the U21 programme, the role focuses on maximising the development and progression of players, supporting their transition into the senior game, and ensuring alignment between the Academy and First Team. Working collaboratively across departments, the postholder will contribute to the continuous evolution of the Academy's technical and performance programmes, helping to create a seamless pathway for emerging talent.

Responsibilities

The u21 Head Coach must: 

Experience
•  Experience working with Professional Development Phase (u18-u21) aged players. 
•  Experience of successfully holding a leadership role or position within a Club or organisation. 
•  Experience of successfully supporting the development of people

Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications
•  To hold appropriate and up to date qualifications to conform to PL Academy Licence requirements. 
•  UEFA A License (FA Level 4 qualification). 
•  FA Advanced Youth Award (FA Level 4 qualification). 
•  Broad awareness of the football industry and governing policies. 
•  An understanding of player development principles or applied knowledge from across other sports, countries and/or clubs

Personal Qualities
•  To ensure the highest levels of professionalism in organisation, delivery and conduct. 
•  To demonstrate an engaging personality that naturally supports the learning and education of players and staff. 
•  To demonstrate growth mindset. 
•  To be Player or Person-Centred in the approach to development. 
•  To show diligence towards all aspects of the role. 
•  To have an outstanding work ethic. 
•  To actively demonstrate humility and vulnerability within the working environment.

Requirements

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role: 
 
Coaching
  • Establish and continually refine the Season Plan for the u21 age group, shaping the player development programme in line with individual player and group needs. 
  • Lead coaching sessions across the u21 age group which align and integrate Season Plan commitments & players Individual Learning Plans (ILPs) to wider Academy and Club approaches and Values.
  • Create and sustain an elite learning environment that appropriately balances challenge and support, empowering players to take ownership of their development and become independent decision-makers.
  • Manage the u21 Games Programme in line with the Season Plan to ensure teams and players compete and develop appropriately through these experiences. 
  • Ensure all training and match experiences are purposefully designed to accelerate individual player development whilst maintaining alignment with the Academy Performance Plan and Club playing philosophy.
  • Lead weekly u21 Multi-Disciplinary Team (MDT) meetings to shape and guide player development while ensuring the highest quality operations and organisation of resource. 
  • Integrate and connect the u21 group to both the u18 and First Team programmes. 
  • Maintain close alignment with First Team staff to ensure shared coaching language, tactical principles, behavioural expectations and physical demands that facilitate seamless player transition.
  • Support the u21 MDT (including u21 Assistant Coach) to integrate player development across disciplines. 
  • Plan, upload/record and reflect systematically on all coaching activity within the u21 age group. 
  • Support the delivery of u16 & u18 training and games programme to share ideas and approaches across the department, contribute to effective succession planning, and cover coaching colleagues as required.
  • Continually evaluate and innovate coaching practice by integrating current research, emerging methodologies and reflective practice to enhance player and programme development.
 
Player & Programme Management 
  • Develop and sustain frequent, consistent and supportive communication with all players, and where appropriate their families and other stakeholders, to support transitions into Professional Football. 
  • Oversee the implementation of the Academy Code of Expectations for all u21s players and staff.
  • Oversee the implementation of all Club policies that relate to the U21s programme. 
  • Lead all u21 player reviews, iteratively contributing to an on-going, continuous process of support for the u21 age group. 
  • Drive individual player acceleration through bespoke development planning, ensuring each player is appropriately challenged and supported in pursuit of First Team and professional football opportunities.
  • Manage the completion of ILPs for all u21 players in collaboration with other disciplines and stakeholders. 
  • Coordinate multidisciplinary contributions to ensure each player's development programme is integrated, evidence-informed and aligned to individual needs.
  • Manage on-going reflection processes (of players and staff) in a way that contributes to on-going learning and development. 
  • Work with the Talent Identification and Recruitment team to provide suitable feedback to any players that trial with the u21s. 
  • Be an available point of contact for First Team colleagues, ensuring there is appropriate and regular connections on u21 players and the u21 programme. 
  • Provide informed recommendations regarding player progression, First Team integration, external loan opportunities and succession planning through regular collaboration with Academy and First Team staff.
  • Player a key role in the Succession Planning processes within the Academy to support the Club to retain individuals who have First Team potential.
  • Foster an elite performance culture that promotes accountability, professionalism, resilience and behaviours consistent with the Club's Values and Code of Expectations.
  • Attendance at First Team games as required.
 
Insights (in collaboration with the Insights department)
  • Align video to team and individual commitments, supporting team and individual player development over time. 
  • Manage all reporting systems to ensure accurate information is captured in relation to player performance. 
  • Ensure all players are provided with regular access to their personal performance data highlighting key metrics in line with the Academy Technical Plan. 
  • Utilise objective performance data, video analysis and observational insights to evaluate programme effectiveness, inform coaching interventions and support evidence-based decision making.
  • Support the development and integration of Insights staff within the u21 MDT. 
 
Leadership & Collaboration
  • Lead, support and positively influence the wider Academy coaching team through collaboration, mentoring and the sharing of best practice across the Professional Development Phase.
  • Build and maintain effective relationships with all Academy departments to ensure a connected, player-centred and high-performing multidisciplinary environment.
  • Contribute to the ongoing evolution of the Academy Technical Plan by identifying opportunities for continuous improvement and innovation across the programme.
  • Act as an ambassador for Fulham Football Club, consistently demonstrating the Club's Values of being Pioneers, Confident Custodians, Action Orientated, Open & Inclusive and committed to Service Excellence.

Benefits

The closing date for applications is Friday 14th August.

job.title: Foundation Safeguarding Manager
job.html_description:
In this role, we’re looking for someone with clear vision and depth of knowledge to support Fulham Football Club Foundation in achieving the objectives of the safeguarding strategy. Someone who will make positive changes that are felt across the Foundation and football industry. To do that, you’ll be well versed in safeguarding best practice, which you’ll then communicate with credibility to the Foundation workforce. 

The post will be responsible for the oversight and direct provision of all safeguarding activities and associated training across the foundation. It is key that there is a Foundation-wide awareness of current football regulations and safeguarding best practice in respect of safeguarding whilst promoting a culture of equality and inclusion. The successful candidate will also be an active advocate of safeguarding for the Foundation internally and externally.


Responsibilities

•  Conduct regular observations of activity and site visits which include working irregular hours, such as evening and some weekends ensuring that safeguarding practices are embedded in delivery.  
•  To support the Head of Safeguarding, ensuring the Foundation and its staff are fully compliant with all safeguarding legislation, Premier League, EFL and FA guidance and to embed safeguarding into the culture of the Foundation. 
•  Work closely with both the Safeguarding and Equality Diversity and Inclusion leads to ensure the Foundation is providing a safe and inclusive environment.
•  Ensure that new staff/ volunteers are embedding safeguarding practices in delivery during induction period 
•  Oversee and develop the Quality Assurance provision in partnership with the Head of Safeguarding and Director of Operations, focusing on the high-risk areas of the Foundation’s delivery to ensure that front line staff are equipped to put safeguarding at the forefront of their delivery and responsibilities. 
•  To support programme leads with the running of Youth Voice, to ensure that children and young people and vulnerable adults are heard and their views on safeguarding and latest trends are taken into account. 
•  Address concerns reported on the Foundations safeguarding reporting system, CPOMS. Lead monthly meetings with senior leaders to review reports. 
•  Support the Head of Safeguarding with the incident and near miss reporting process across the Foundation ensuring thorough investigations are carried out and escalated through appropriate channels.
•  Using CPOMS, track data in relation to incidents, accidents and complaints, identify patterns and trends to inform organisational direction. Act as lead Foundation official and lead on or support the Head of Safeguarding in any investigation of an allegation of abuse or poor practice.
•  Work closely with the Foundation’s participants, coaches and staff (operations, programmes, training, observations)
•  Oversight of safeguarding recording on CPOMS including the monitoring, analysis and evaluation.
•  To work with the Head of Safeguarding and HR to ensure that all staff/volunteers who are working with children and young people are DBS checked and attend a safeguarding induction and regular safeguarding workshops. 
•  Work closely with HR to ensure that the single central record for each activity at the Foundation that involves Children and/or Adults at Risk is maintained, including relevant and permitted Disclosure information, safeguarding training records and any other information relevant to Safeguarding Vulnerable Groups. 
•  Conduct regular spot check audits throughout the year to assess compliance with safeguarding standards. 
•  Provide advice and guidance to the HR Department (and other departments as required) on all safeguarding related legislation.
•  Support staff in the sign-off process of planning off-site activities, trips, residentials and events.
•  Ensure that all third parties and partners that the Foundation engage with are compliant with safeguarding legislation and league standards. 
•  Ensure sensitive information is held securely, is GDPR compliant and all safeguarding and wellbeing concerns are recorded on our electronic case management system. 
•  Contribute to successful relationships with the English Football League, Premier League, FA and support other collaborations with agencies such as schools, education, social services, the Police and Youth Offending Teams. 
•  To advise on Foundation external activities including match day activities in relation to safeguarding.
•  To lead on keeping the organisation up to date and in line with legislation and communications around policies and processes associated with safeguarding activity.
•  To support the Head of Safeguarding and Director of Safeguarding and Inclusion to ensure the Foundation reaches its potential on all relevant safeguarding audits and be accountable for audit recommendations being monitored, reviewed and implemented. 
•  Provide relevant advice and guidance and embed best practice as appropriate.
•  Execute additional tasks as required in order to meet the Foundation’s changing priorities.
•  Champion and provide a vocal presence for Mental Health & Wellbeing within the Foundation;
•  Attend Mental Health & Wellbeing related working groups/action groups and offer operational perspective as and when required, and share information and communicate progress/issues back to colleagues;
•  Attend Foundation forums to share information and promote the safety of young people;
•  Work respectfully, sensitively and empathically with people with poor mental health and/or illness at all times;
•  Support any requests for updates on activities undertaken by the organisation around mental health.


Requirements

Essential
Experience:
•  Experience in social work, teaching or a related field working with children and/or adults at risk. Must have a background/experience in safeguarding preferably in a youth setting.
•  Recent experience of working effectively with external agencies, local community and a governing body.
•  Experienced in managing safeguarding concerns and keeping clear and comprehensive records of incidents.
•  Ability to contribute to the implementation and regular updating of policies and procedures for the safeguarding of children and ‘adults at risk’ across all areas of the club.

Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
Knowledge of:
•  The current safeguarding challenges in football/sport.
•  The UK safeguarding best practice.

Skills
•  Exceptional communication skills – both oral and written (presentation skills and delivery of ideas)
•  Commitment to collaborative and consultative working.
•  An understanding of the importance of, and the desire to engage with and inspire young people whatever their challenges.
•  The ability to deal sensitively with complex problems that can arise in child protection issues and/or similar matters.
•  A proven ability to manage change and to establish and maintain good working relationships with staff, children, young people, parents and ‘adults at risk’ – ability to work well with others is vital.
•  Experience of providing training and development for staff.
•  Excellent organisational skills, ability to effectively manage competing priorities and adhere to a range of tight deadlines.
•  High degree of professionalism and integrity, who will uphold the values of the Foundation. 

Qualifications
  • Relevant safeguarding qualification - appropriate experience will be accepted as an alternative.
  • Evidence of on-going CPD.

Desirable
Experience:
  • A track record in overseeing safeguarding arrangements for ‘adults at risk.’

Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
Knowledge of:
•  The impact of EDI on Safeguarding practices.
•  ‘Prevent’ including extremist and terrorist groups. 
•  Safeguarding, safer recruitment and equality and diversity practice.

Skills
•  Working in a similar role, ideally in a governing or membership body within sport or other suitable industry.
•  Demonstrable experience of strategies to raise standards; an aptitude and enthusiasm for effective analysis of data and its use in setting targets for improvement.

Qualifications
•  Degree or equivalent level qualification or experience.

job.title: Pre-Academy & Development Centre Head Coach (Slough)
job.html_description:
1. To lead on the development of all talent and support Recruitment Managers by providing insight on player progress
  2. To lead on the organisation, management and setup of practices at your relevant centre 

Responsibilities

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role:
  • To ensure the high quality co-ordination and smooth operational running of the session you lead at your respective Pre-Academy or development centre session.
 
  • To ensure the deployment of appropriate football & sports coaches onto sessions. 
 
  • To collaborate effectively with the relevant Recruitment Manager manager to ensure a safe and fun programme for our young players. 
 
  • When required, to effectively support the running and development of the clubs Pre Academy at Motspur Park. 
 
  • To collaborate effectively with the wider academy team, driving high standards, sharing best practice and establishing strong opportunities for participant transitions between programmes. 
 
  • To identify talent and organise coach delivery at your centre or session, whilst attending any mandatory meetings. 
 
  • To manage registers, databases and spectators at the venue and provide feedback to parents when appropriate. 
 
  • To safeguard all personnel when the centre is running and correctly dismiss and welcome children upon arrival.

Requirements

The Pre-Academy & Development Centre Head Coach must have: 
  • Experience working in a sports participation-based environment 
  • Experience of managing projects coaching football to young people, specifically primary school aged children.
  • Experience working as an individual as well as part of a team. 
  • Experience working with Microsoft Office
  • Hold a UEFA C License/FA Level 2 Coaching in Football
  • FA First Aid Qualification
  • FA Safeguarding Children in Football Qualification
 
Ideally, the Pre-Academy & Development Centre Head will: 
  • Have worked in a Pre-Academy or Academy Development Centre
  • Have worked in an Academy setting
  • Have completed FA Talent ID Level 1 in Introduction to Scouting 
  • Have experience working in Scouting & Talent Identification

job.title: Matchday Groundsperson Casual
job.html_description:
The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role:

• Repair works to the pitch in the form of divoting after warm up’s, half time and post-match use.
• Post-match pedestrian mowing using rotary and cylinder mowers.
• Setting up grow lights and moving them from storage compound into stadium post-game when required.
• Washing and cleaning of machinery after usage.
• Comply with all Health and Safety regulations and requirements within the Company and your role.
• Drive vehicles and handle equipment as required for grounds maintenance operations.
• Establish and maintain effective working relationships with managers, colleagues and end users, ensure grounds management are kept informed of any issues that may be identified.
• Undertaking general maintenance operations associated with pitch.
• Work within a stadium team to ensure the upkeep of the stadium pitch.
• This job description does not contain all the duties and responsibilities that may arise in this role, you will need to undertake other duties as instructed and use initiative to ensure the safe operational functioning of the stadium.
• Expectation is to work at least 75% of home fixtures.

job.title: Female Football Coach (Casual)
job.plain_text_description:
Fulham FC Foundation are currently seeking to recruit an enthusiastic and committed person to take up the casual position of a Female Football Coach.
Reporting directly to our Operations Officers the Female Football Coach will be responsible for managing a number of female teams at one of the foundations partner schools. This role would involve both the management of these teams, as well as providing high-quality, team-based training sessions throughout the week. You will also be responsible for overseeing any fixtures these team have across the season. This is a casual role where flexibility is essential, as the delivery of training sessions and fixtures changes across the school term.
The successful candidate will be somebody who has prior experience managing a female team, and holds at least a UEFA C License qualification. Due to the requirements stipulated by the school, the successful candidate will be a female coach with relatable experience to their players allowing them to be a positive role model to them.
Although this role is casual, with the hours varying across the season, meaning that there is no set timetable. There are some key times when training sessions and fixtures are likely to happen. Therefore, the ideal candidate will have good availability during the afternoons of the working week. The ideal availability will be:
Monday – Friday from 2pm to 6pm
There will also be opportunity to work across other foundation programmes such as our ‘Player Development Centres’ and ‘Girls Development Centres’ should the successful candidate want to.
Whilst there is no obligation for Fulham FC Foundation to provide, or for the Female Football Coaches to accept, work. Female Football Coaches who do not work for an extended period of time (3 months), may no longer be offered work.
Salary: £16.50 p/h
Next steps:
The closing date for this role is the 30th of June, however applications will be reviewed consistently so any appropriate candidate may be interviewed before this date.
If successful, you will join a vibrant team who are passionate about achieving the organisation's vision of “an active healthy, inclusive and thriving community”, and you’ll have the opportunity to build on your existing skills through a variety of training and development opportunities and experiences. This role will also play a role in supporting the Foundation’s Women’s and Girls Strategy to develop and support opportunities for underrepresented groups.
*This job description should not be regarded as exclusive or exhaustive. It is intended as an outline indication of areas of activity and responsibility and will be amended in the light of the changing needs of the organisation.
Responsibilities
- To act as an Ambassador for Fulham FC Foundation (FFCF), representing the organisation professionally in line with its values.
- To design and deliver high quality, team training sessions to the teams you’ll be working with.
- To manage the teams during both home and away fixtures, including all the team admin that does along with managing the team.
- To provide high-quality, individualised feedback to each of the players in your teams to support their footballing development.
- To be a positive role model to the student athletes, helping both motivate and support them with their football, and education.
- To identify and support progression pathways for talented young people.
- To provide a safe, positive and inclusive learning environment at all times,
- To adhere to FFCF’s safeguarding policies and procedures, ensuring the timely reporting of any safeguarding concerns or incidents within sessions.
Requirements
Essential:
Experience:
- Experience of delivering high quality training sessions to female footballers. - Experience of running a 9 or 11 aside female football team. - Experience of working with others as part of a coaching team. - Has a driving license and/or is willing to travel independently.
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
- Excellent verbal communication skills. - Excellent knowledge of Women’s Football. - Excellent knowledge of the pathway opportunities for female players. - First Aid, Safeguarding and DBS qualification. - A UEFA C Coaching Qualification, or currently undertaking and due to complete this year. - Base knowledge of and willingness to learn & contribute towards FFCF strategic aims.
Personal Qualities:
- A positive role-model for children & young people. - Ability to travel independently across Surrey and South-West London, including transport of equipment. - Well presented, with a professional manner. - Positive, energetic persona. Able to build rapport with participants. - Excellent time-keeping & punctuality. - Willingness to learn & develop personally & professionally.
Preferred:
Experience:
- Experience of delivering football sessions in a secondary school - Experience of working with high performing footballers. - Experience of leading a local female grassroots team
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
- Additional football qualifications such as Goalkeeping, S&C, or Fitness. - Knowledge and links to local grassroots football teams. - UEFA B License (or willing to work towards)

job.title: Host Family
job.html_description:
Are you passionate about football and looking for a unique opportunity to make a difference in the lives of young athletes, aged 15-21?


Fulham FC is seeking warm and welcoming host families to provide a safe and supportive home environment to support our Academy players who will be required to live away from home to fulfil their education and football training at our club.


As a host parent, you will play an essential role in helping our players thrive both on and off the pitch. You'll provide a comfortable living space, home-cooked meals, emotional support and help them to adjust to life away from home as they focus on their training and academic pursuits.


What we are looking for:
  • A friendly, caring family or individual with a spare room
  • A willingness to provide support, guidance, and encouragement to our young players
  • A safe and welcoming home environment
  • Support our young people by teaching them basic independent living and self-care skills such as washing, cooking and cleaning up after themselves.
  • Providing meals in line with nutritional guidance from the Academy.
  • Accommodation has access to public and local amenities with good transport links to the Academy training ground.
  • Report any welfare concerns to the Academy Safeguarding and Player Care team should they occur.
  • Include our young people in family life as much as they feel comfortable with.
  • The club will regularly inspect and visit the placement during the season.
  • The club will provide further guidance to host families, young people and their parents explaining what would be expected of them.

In order to be considered for this position you must live within 30 minutes travel for the player from the training ground.

Fulham Football Club is committed to safeguarding and ensuring the welfare and protection of children and young people and expects host families to share this commitment. As such, the host family provider will be subject to an Enhanced Disclosure & Barring Service (DBS) check and risk assessments prior to a placement commencing.


Any other person over the age of 18, who resides in the household or has regular contact with the player will be required to complete an enhanced DBS. Host Families will be required to attend safeguarding training and workshops arranged by the Academy.


We are committed to supporting an environment where all staff have a personal responsibility to uphold the Club’s Equal Opportunities Policy by treating fellow employees, prospective employees, casual workers, prospective casual workers, players, prospective players and customers fairly and impartially.

job.title: Maintenance Engineer - Electrician
job.html_description:
We are looking for an experienced Electrician to provide a comprehensive high standard of Maintenance support to the Club and proactively identify areas for improvement and develop and implement solutions.

Responsibilities

The Maintenance Engineer – Electrician must: 
  • Experience of electrical installation within a large commercial environment 
  • NVQ level 1, 2, 3 in Electrical Installation
  • 18th Edition

Ideally, Maintenance Engineer – Electrician will: 
  • Experience in previous Maintenance roles
  • Experience using Planned Maintenance software 
  • Full Driving Licence
  • PAT testing experience
  • Proven ability to work unsupervised and as part of a team
  • Proactive
  • Organised
  • Flexible Attitude
  • Team Player 

Requirements

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role: 
  • To carry out electrical work, both reactive and planned maintenance
  • To carry out general day to day maintenance duties, which will sometimes be on very tight deadlines and to a high-level finish
  • General planned maintenance is divided between the team dependant on site coverage
  • Site electrical installations and upgrade works
  • Assist in ad-hoc projects where required
  • Matchday preparation carried out 24-72hrs prior to each game
  • Matchday & Event cover along with other team members
  • To ensure that all work is carried out in a safe manner and within relevant Health and Safety Guidelines
  • Covering Events where required 

Benefits

Applications close on 21st August.

job.title: Football & Sports Coach - Development Centres
job.html_description:
To deliver high quality football coaching sessions to accomplished & aspiring grassroots players aged 6 to 16.

To deliver football & sports sessions across the wider Foundation to a range of children, young people and adults.


Responsibilities

  • To act as an Ambassador for FFCF and maintain and develop relationships to ensure high quality experiences for young people, partner organisations, other staff and customers

  • To effectively plan and deliver high quality football sessions in-line with coaching syllabus, philosophy and values

  • To effectively support the development of individual players through the creation of individual development plans throughout the season

  • To identify and support the development of progression pathways for talented young people

  • To effectively plan and deliver extra-curricular and community activities across the wider Foundation

  • To support the transition between school-based activities, wider Foundation activities and where appropriate, other community activities

  • Assist in data collection and completion of monitoring for reports on an ongoing basis, within the timescales required

  • To work closely with Football Development Officer's to understand programme standards and attendance targets and support the promotion of FFCF activities

  • To support the smooth function of the Operations Department in line with the Foundation values and targets and work across programmes, when required

Requirements

Essential:

Experience:
  • Leading football sessions to age groups U7 to U16
  • Delivery of extracurricular and community activities to all age groups
  • Supporting and developing coaches in a sports environment
  • Working with external partners to achieve successful outcome
  • Monitoring and Evaluation 
  • Marketing and promotion

Skills, knowledge & qualifications:
  • Minimum of UEFA C qualification in Coaching Football
  • FA First Aid - in date
  • FA Safeguarding - in date
  • Ability to drive, has access to a car or ability to travel independently

Personal qualities:
  • Committed and motivated by the purpose of the Foundation 
  • Demonstrates respect for colleagues, partners and customers and when possible operates above and beyond expectations
  • Well presented with a good manner
  • Excellent punctuality
  • Ability to prioritise work and consistently meet deadlines
  • Effective communicator
  • Cheerful positive attitude

Preferred:

Experience:
  • Delivery in a Club Community Organisation (CCO)
  • Delivery of activiry to young people with a Disability. 
  • Delivery of CPD events to coaches.
  • Delivery of Physical Education lessons to primary age children

Skills, knowledge ​& qualifications:
  • UEFA B qualification
  • Non-football NGB sports qualifications
  • Mentoring qualification
  • Talent Identification qualification
  • Understanding of Physical Education standards in schools (Ofsted guidance)

job.title: Lewisham Advanced Centre Coach
job.html_description:
Join our team at the Lewisham Advanced Centre and play a key role in shaping the next generation of talent. Working closely alongside the Head Coach and a dedicated team of coaches, you will contribute to the development, support, and progression of players in a dynamic and professional environment.

This is an opportunity to make a real impact, delivering high-quality coaching, fostering player growth, and creating a positive, high-performance culture.

As a representative of Fulham FC, you will be expected to consistently uphold and embody the club’s core values in everything you do, both on and off the pitch.

Responsibilities

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
  • Deliver high-quality coaching and player development across both the Lewisham Advanced Centre and Motspur Park, ensuring every session meets the highest professional standards.
  • Work collaboratively with the Head Coach, Pre-Academy Manager, and Recruitment Manager to create a safe, engaging, and enjoyable environment for all young players.
  • Provide effective support in the delivery and ongoing development of the club’s Pre-Academy programme at Motspur Park, contributing to its continued growth and success.
  • Build strong working relationships with the wider academy team, promoting high standards, sharing best practice, and creating clear, supportive pathways for players transitioning between programmes.
  • Attend and contribute to internal and external meetings as required, representing the programme with professionalism and purpose.
  • Maintain a strong focus on safeguarding at all times—ensuring all participants are safely welcomed and dismissed, and that a secure, supportive environment is consistently upheld.

Requirements

  • FA Level 1 Coaching qualification, with up-to-date FA First Aid and Safeguarding certifications.
  • IT literate, with proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Highly organised, with strong time management and planning skills.
  • Good knowledge of coaching standards and best practice.
  • Clear and effective communication skills.
  • Committed to safeguarding, equality, diversity, and inclusion in the workplace.

job.title: Stadium Tour Guide - Weekend
job.html_description:
We intend on building the Craven Cottage stadium tour to be one of the truly popular London experiences for football fans and visitors to London. Our guides are key to this objective. 
Craven Cottage tour guides are expected to be hard working, well presented, passionate and dedicated to ensuring that our guest’s expectations are met every time. Guides are also expected to be proactive and receptive to performance feedback and to be enthusiastic, proud club ambassadors in every possible aspect of the position.

Responsibilities

PERSON SPECIFICATION AND ATTRIBUTES
 
  • Smart and well presented
  • Guest oriented
  • Positive attitude
  • Friendly, flexible and proactive
  • Strong team player with the ability and willingness to work alone
  • Knowledgeable and passionate regarding Craven Cottage and Fulham Football Club
  • Willing to improve and develop
  • Reliable and punctual
  • High personal standards
  • Values and respects others
  • Takes responsibility
  • Ideally a Fulham fan but this is not essential
  • The ability and willingness to work home match days if required
  • The willingness to wear official club branded clothes as directed by the stadium   tour manager when leading tours or on duty.
  • The ability to regularly work weekends


Skills and Experience
 
  • Excellent communication skills with  the confidence to speak to large groups
  • Customer service skills with the desire to improve
  • The ability to study and learn the history of the club and ground
  • The ability to present the information to the timings required in an interesting, passionate manner and with   historical accuracy
  • The ability and interest in remaining up to date with the latest club news
  • Where necessary, the willingness and ability to work in an office environment, responding to emails, answering enquiries, selling tickets for the tour and tour events.

Requirements

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • To support the delivery of the Craven Cottage stadium tour, across all   operations and in every respect
  • To deliver an engaging stadium tour to a wide variety of guests
  • To handle payments
  • Provide a customer service experience to our guests that meets their expectations
  • To deliver a personable tour, including welcoming and saying goodbye to the   group
  • To deal with a wide variety of customer enquiries
  • To be a proud and enthusiastic club ambassador
  • Taking photo’s where requested for guests where and when permitted
  • To liase with stadium management, stadium tour manager and security on a tour   day and while the tour is in progress where necessary
  • Ensure that the tour route is litter free, clear, safe and adheres to health and   safety policies and procedures
  • To promote the club at every opportunity including ticketing, retail,   hospitality and events
  • Deliver other tours relevant to Fulham Football Club
  • To carry out other related duties that may reasonably be required including   covering for absent staff during holidays and sickness
  • To be responsible for the safety and security of staff, visitors and the ground   throughout the tour and while guests are present in the stadium. This   includes following instructions from the stadium tour manager, security,   stadium management and other departments

Benefits

Full training will be provided to the successful applicant.

This is a casual position and hours will be arranged accordingly.

Shifts will involve weekend, weekdays, bank holidays and potentially match days. Hours might involve evening shifts or early starts when required. The length of the shift may vary according to the needs of the organisation and events.

job.title: Academy Therapist (Casual)
job.html_description:
To deliver high-quality physiotherapy services across the Foundation Phase (FP) and Youth Development Phase (YDP) squads (U9–U16) within a multidisciplinary team environment. Provide medical support on match days, during clinics, and at tournaments, ensuring optimal care and performance outcomes for academy players. Assist in the implementation of injury prevention strategies and rehabilitation programmes aimed at maximising performance, enhancing recovery, and minimising injury risk. Support the effective transition of players from the FP and YDP into the Professional Development Phase (PDP) by contributing to a comprehensive and cohesive medical pathway.

Responsibilities

The therapist will play a key role in the delivery of medical services to academy players across the Foundation and Youth Development Phases. Working as part of a multidisciplinary team, they will support all aspects of injury management, contribute to player development through preventative care strategies, and ensure effective communication and documentation across all stakeholders.

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role:
 • Provide medical cover for FP and YDP players during match days (primarily Sundays, with some midweek fixtures), evening clinics, and domestic or international tournaments. 
  • Support the assessment, treatment, and rehabilitation of injuries in collaboration with the full-time U9–U16 physiotherapist, ensuring appropriate return-to-play protocols are followed. 
  • Contribute to the planning and delivery of injury prevention strategies, including individual and group-based sessions tailored to player needs. 
  • Liaise effectively with coaching staff to support player load management during key stages of physical development. 
  • Communicate and coordinate with parents, external medical providers (NHS/private), and internal staff to facilitate appropriate ongoing care. 
  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date medical records on the PMA system and ensure clear handovers between staff for all FP and YDP players. 
  • Assist in the transition of players from FP/YDP into the PDP phase by sharing relevant medical and movement history with appropriate personnel. 
  • Engage in internal CPD, contribute to research and development within paediatric sports medicine, and undertake relevant professional development to support continuous improvement.

Requirements

The Casual Academy Therapist must:
  • BSc degree in Physiotherapy, Sports Therapy, Sports Rehabilitation. 
  • Be a member of the appropriate governing body – CSP, SST, BASRaT 
  • FA Level 4 ITMMiF • Experience working in a sports medicine environment.
  • Experience working in a multidisciplinary team. 
  • FA Safegurading • Be able to work as part of a team 
  • Available to work on a flexible basis including evening and weekends

Ideally, the Casual Academy Therapist will:
  • FA Level 5 ATMMiF
  • Experience and understanding of paediatric sports medicine 
  • Experience working within a Category 1 football academy

- Support the assessment, treatment, and rehabilitation of injuries in collaboration with the full-time U9–U16 physiotherapist, ensuring appropriate return-to-play protocols are followed. - Contribute to the planning and delivery of injury prevention strategies, including individual and group-based sessions tailored to player needs. - Liaise effectively with coaching staff to support player load management during key stages of physical development. - Communicate and coordinate with parents, external medical providers (NHS/private), and internal staff to facilitate appropriate ongoing care. - Maintain accurate, up-to-date medical records on the PMA system and ensure clear handovers between staff for all FP and YDP players. - Assist in the transition of players from FP/YDP into the PDP phase by sharing relevant medical and movement history with appropriate personnel. - Engage in internal CPD, contribute to research and development within paediatric sports medicine, and undertake relevant professional development to support continuous improvement.
Requirements
The Casual Academy Therapist must:
- BSc degree in Physiotherapy, Sports Therapy, Sports Rehabilitation. - Be a member of the appropriate governing body – CSP, SST, BASRaT - FA Level 4 ITMMiF • Experience working in a sports medicine environment. - Experience working in a multidisciplinary team. - FA Safegurading • Be able to work as part of a team - Available to work on a flexible basis including evening and weekends
Ideally, the Casual Academy Therapist will:
- FA Level 5 ATMMiF - Experience and understanding of paediatric sports medicine - Experience working within a Category 1 football academy

job.title: Warehouse Operative/Driver (Part-time)

job.title: Academy Scout
job.html_description:
The Academy Scout (Local Recruitment) plays a vital role in identifying and monitoring talented young players within the local area, whether from grassroots clubs or other academies.


Working as part of the local Academy scouting team, you will be responsible for producing detailed player reports, sharing insights with Academy staff, and contributing to a comprehensive understanding of the player landscape within your assigned region.


We have a particular interest in recruiting scouts with strong networks and knowledge within the following areas:

  • Grassroots: South London, West London

  • Professional Academies: East London, North London

Responsibilities

• Manage your individual weekend schedule and attend fixtures within your allocated region or phase.
• Observe and report on players demonstrating potential within your area and age phase.
• Network with other local scouts to exchange information and intelligence on potential targets.
• Keep Local Recruitment Managers updated on high-potential players within your area.
• Support communication with families of players involved in Talent ID programmes and trial processes.
• Assist in the delivery of Talent ID events and scouting programmes as required.
• Contribute to scouting team meetings to review succession planning and player targets.
• Attend department meetings, CPD sessions, and all required safeguarding training.

Requirements

• Strong knowledge and network within your designated local area.
• Previous experience scouting for another Academy (Category 1, 2, or 3).
• FA Talent ID Level 1 qualification.
• FA Safeguarding certification.

job.title: Fire Officer
job.html_description:
Position Purpose 

 

The Fire Team will not normally be expected to be involved in the management of spectators. When deployed as a member of the Fire Team the primary is one of fire prevention and first response should an outbreak of fire occur.
This role is suitable for candidates who are or have experience of the fire industry or stewards who are willing to undergo additional fire safety training to enable them to carry out this role.

Responsibilities

  • Attend the Stadium at given dates and times as dictated by the Head of Safety.
  • Undertake pre-match and post-match fire checks as instructed by the Fire Team leader. Arrive at Steward Sign as directed.
  • Conduct Pre-Match Checks and specified documentation on Raven Controls as required.
  • Conduct patrols within the stand and under croft’s to minimise the risk of fire breaking out and assisting to prevent the spread of fire. 
  • Respond to Fire and associated incidents as directed by FFC Control, ensuring staff are supported, appropriate action is taken, and that information is passed to the Safety Management Team in FFC Control (Act – Inform – Escalate)
  • Attend during match meetings with Fire Team leader for the identification of issues to be addressed, learning points and review of specific deployments. 
  • Report any fire safety concerns to the fire team leader for appropriate action and escalation to FFC Control and the Safety Officer. 
  • Know the location of and be able to effectively operate the firefighting equipment at the Stadium. 
  • Be able to provide basic ‘First Aid’ if required. 
  • Know the location of the First Aid Rooms located within the Stadium. 
  • Be fully conversant with any methods or messages used to alert staff that an emergency has arisen. 
  • Be capable of recognising potential fire hazards and items of interest or suspect packages, reporting such matters immediately to the Fire Team leader, a Supervisor, Chief Steward, Deputy Safety Officer, or Safety Officer. 
  • Promptly comply with any instruction given by a Supervisor, Chief Steward, Deputy Safety Officer, Safety Officer, or Police Officer. 
  • Comply with the relevant instructions and guidance contained in the Stewards Handbook and standing instructions for the FFC Fire Team. 
  • Attend all required training. 
  • To understand their general responsibilities towards the health and safety and welfare of all spectators, other stewards, staff, and themselves.


Essential and Desirable 
 
Background in Fire industry (present/previous Fire Service) and willing to undergo relevant training. 

Requirements

To act in accordance with the general recommendations of the Guide to Safety at Sports Ground (Green Guide) and the specific requirements of the Safety Certificate issued by the Local Authority under the Safety of Sports Ground Act 1975. Fire Safety Officers play a key role in the event day safety team ensuring that the stadium provides a safe and secure environment for thousands of visitors. You will become a focal point for all fire safety issues, providing preventative advice and measures in an emergency.

 

  • You should be a minimum of 18 years of age, be fit, active and have the character and temperament to carry out the duties required. 
  • You should possess good communication skills.
  • You must be able to attend most first-team home fixtures and other major events held at the stadium.
  • You should be polite, courteous, and helpful to all supporters.
  • Whilst on duty you will adhere to the Club dress code and be clean and tidy.
  • You are not engaged to watch the game but are expected to concentrate on your area of responsibility. 
  • You should never show hostility or use obscene or offensive language to any supporters.
  • You should never act in any way likely to bring discredit on the Club.

job.title: Casual DisAbility Football & Sports Coach
job.plain_text_description:
Fulham FC Foundation are currently seeking to recruit an enthusiastic and committed person to take up the casual position of DisAbility Football & Sports Coach.
Reporting directly to our Senior DisAbility Development Manager, the DisAbility Football & Sports Coaches are responsible for delivering high-quality football & sports coaching to children, young people and adults with disabilities and additional needs. This role involves delivery across a wide-range of our DisAbility Programmes, including Pan DisAbility Clubs, Active Autism, Down’s Syndrome ‘Badgers’, Blind and Partially Sighted, Cerebral Palsy and Dwarfism Football Sessions. In addition there will be opportunities to work in our DisAbility Schools programme delivering PE, Enrichment Activities and After School Clubs.
While the primary focus of this role is on DisAbility Football & Sport, there may be opportunities to contribute to other FFC Foundation activities such as Skills Club, Development Centres, Soccer Schools, Primary Education, Kicks, and Health & Wellbeing. We would encourage candidates to prioritise DisAbility Programmes where possible, while remaining flexible to support other areas as needed.
This is a casual role where flexibility is essential, as the role necessitates involvement in supporting the delivery of programme activities as and when required.
The successful candidate will be somebody who has prior experience delivering football & sports coaching sessions to children & young people with disabilities or additional needs in grassroots & school settings, holds at least a FA Level 1/Introduction to Coaching Football qualification and is committed to the charitable purpose of Fulham FC Foundation.
As this role is casual, there is no set timetable. Sessions may be offered on an adhoc or regular basis, depending on the needs of Fulham FC Foundation. It is the responsibility of the DisAbility Football & Sports Coaches to maintain consistent and effective communication with our Senior DisAbility Development Manager and Operations Officers to ensure the continuation of work.
Whilst there is no obligation for Fulham FC Foundation to provide, or for the DisAbility Football & Sports Coaches to accept, work. DisAbility Football & Sports Coaches who do not work for an extended period of time, will be deactivated.
The successful candidates should be available to work across at least one of the below times, in order to receive work. We are extremely keen to hear from those who are able to work on Saturday mornings.
Weekdays – 9am to 5 pm;
Weekday Evenings – 5pm to 9pm
Weekends – Saturdays – 8am to 12noon.
Work in other timings is available, however on a far reduced frequency.
Salary Range: £12.95 p/h to £16.50 p/h
Next steps
:
There is no closing date for this role. Applications will be reviewed on a bi-weekly basis.
If successful, you will join a vibrant team who are passionate about achieving the organisation's vision of “an active, inclusive and thriving community”, and you’ll have the opportunity to build on your existing skills through a variety of training and development opportunities and experiences
*
This job description should not be regarded as exclusive or exhaustive. It is intended as an outline indication of areas of activity and responsibility and will be amended in the light of the changing needs of the organisation
.
Responsibilities
- To act as an Ambassador for Fulham FC Foundation (FFCF), representing the organisation professionally in line with its values. - To plan and deliver high-quality football and sports coaching sessions to children, young people & adults in-line with FFCF standards. - To provide a safe, positive and inclusive learning environment at all times, - To adhere to FFCF’s safeguarding policies and procedures, ensuring the timely reporting of any safeguarding concerns or incidents within sessions. - To engage, include, inspire and grow participation across FFCF activities. - To support the transition of participants between different FFCF programmes and activities. - To champion opportunities for individuals from underrepresented groups within FFCF activities. - To identify and support progression pathways for talented young people. - To support the development of FFCF programmes through positive collaboration with Department Managers / Operations Officers. - To support the promotion of FFCF programmes across the local community. - To assist in data collection and completion of monitoring & evaluation on an ongoing basis.
Requirements
Essential:
Experience:
- Delivery of football coaching sessions in a grassroots environment - Delivery of sports coaching sessions to children, young people or adults with disabilities and additional needs. - Delivery within a school/college setting. - Working in a customer-facing role.
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
- Introduction to Coaching Football qualification - In-date FA Emergency First Aid - In-date FA Safeguarding Children certificate - Base knowledge of and willingness to learn & contribute towards FFCF strategic aims.
Personal Qualities:
- A positive role-model for children & young people. - Ability to travel independently across South-West London, including transport of equipment. - Well presented, with a professional manner. - Positive, energetic persona. Able to build rapport with participants. - Excellent time-keeping & punctuality. - Willingness to learn & develop personally & professionally.
Preferred:
Experience:
- Delivery of football & sports coaching sessions in a Club Community Organisation (CCO). - Delivery of Physical Education within a school setting. - Delivery within a classroom environment. - Marketing & Promoting participation activities in the community. - Delivery of football & sports coaching sessions to females.
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
- FA Level 2/UEFA C in Coaching Football qualification (or higher). - Additional PE/HLTA qualification - Mentoring qualification - Non-football NGB sports qualifications.

• Replenish stock and keep stores and displays tidy and well-presented.
• Price and label products correctly across the store.
• Support the matchday running of the store and assist with additional tasks when required
• Work in various units across the stadium

job.title: Head of Grounds - Craven Cottage
job.html_description:
The Head of Grounds – Craven Cottage is responsible for the leadership, management, preparation and performance of the playing surface and associated grounds operations at Craven Cottage.
 
The postholder is accountable for ensuring that the stadium pitch is maintained and presented to the highest professional standards, providing a safe, consistent and high-performing playing surface for First Team, Women’s and Academy football, together with approved pitch hires, events and other stadium activity.
 
The role will develop and deliver annual pitch maintenance, renovation and improvement programmes, balancing a varied programme of football fixtures and training, commercial use, events, weather conditions and the long-term health and performance of the playing surface.
 
A key responsibility of the role is to manage and advise on pitch usage, working collaboratively with football and commercial stakeholders to maximise appropriate use of the stadium pitch whilst protecting playing quality, recovery periods and the Club’s long-term investment in the surface.
 
The postholder will lead the Craven Cottage grounds team, manage budgets, specialist machinery and pitch infrastructure, and work closely with Football Operations, Stadium Operations, Commercial and Events teams to ensure the playing surface is prepared to the required standard for all approved uses.

Responsibilities

Essential and Desirable
 
Essential Experience
  • Significant experience in professional sports turf management.
  • Experience in the preparation and maintenance of high-quality natural grass playing surfaces.
  • Experience operating within professional football, professional sport or a comparable elite sporting environment.
  • Experience managing playing surfaces subject to varied and intensive usage.
  • Experience leading and developing a grounds team.
  • Experience planning and delivering pitch maintenance and renovation programmes.
  • Experience managing budgets, contractors, machinery and operational resources.
  • Experience managing specialist pitch infrastructure including irrigation and drainage systems.

Essential Skills / Qualifications
  • Relevant qualification in Sports Turf, Horticulture or Grounds Management.
  • Strong technical knowledge of sports turf maintenance and agronomy.
  • Strong understanding of irrigation, drainage, turf machinery and pitch infrastructure.
  • Appropriate pesticide application qualifications relevant to the role.
  • Good working knowledge of Health & Safety requirements associated with grounds operations.
  • Good IT, administrative and record-keeping skills.
  • Strong organisational, planning and communication skills.
  • Ability to make sound operational decisions and balance competing football, commercial and operational demands.

Desirable Experience / Skills / Qualifications
  • Significant experience maintaining a stadium pitch within professional football.
  • NVQ Level 3 or above, or equivalent qualification, in Sports Turf Management.
  • PA1 / PA2 / PA6 or equivalent relevant pesticide qualifications.
  • IOSH or equivalent Health & Safety qualification.
  • Experience of hybrid pitch systems and associated specialist technology.
  • Experience managing major pitch renovation or reconstruction projects.
  • Experience managing playing surfaces used for both elite sport and non-football events.
  • Experience using turf performance monitoring and management information to inform maintenance programmes.

Personal Qualities
  • Exceptionally high standards and attention to detail.
  • Strong leadership and people-management capability.
  • Proactive and solutions focused.
  • Calm and decisive under pressure.
  • Reliable and accountable.
  • Commercially aware and able to balance pitch protection with the wider operational requirements of the Club.
  • Collaborative approach to working with football, commercial and operational departments.
  • Strong work ethic and personal credibility.
  • Flexible approach to working hours in line with fixtures, events and operational demands.

Additional Information 

Due to the nature of professional football and stadium operations, flexibility is required, including evenings, weekends and public holidays where operationally necessary.

Requirements

Grounds & Playing Surface Management

  • Lead all aspects of preparation, maintenance and presentation of the Craven Cottage playing surface.
  • Ensure the pitch is maintained consistently to elite professional football standards.
  • Develop, implement and monitor annual and seasonal turf management programmes.
  • Plan and undertake mowing, aeration, fertilisation, irrigation, overseeding, topdressing, plant health and disease management programmes.
  • Monitor pitch condition and performance through appropriate testing, inspection and record keeping.
  • Monitor weather forecasts and ground conditions and adapt maintenance programmes accordingly.
  • Manage playing surface usage to protect pitch quality, recovery and long-term performance.
  • Maintain the highest standards of pitch presentation, including line marking, goal preparation and matchday set-up.
  • Plan and deliver annual and in-season renovation programmes.

Football, Pitch Use & Events
  • Ensure the playing surface is fully prepared and presented for all First Team home fixtures.
  • Prepare and maintain the playing surface for approved Women’s and Academy fixtures and other football activity at Craven Cottage.
  • Work closely with Football Operations to understand fixture requirements and ensure appropriate preparation and recovery periods.
  • Work with Stadium Operations, Commercial and Events teams in planning pitch hires, events and other approved uses of the playing surface.
  • Assess proposed pitch activity and provide professional advice on its likely impact on surface condition, recovery and future football requirements.
  • Support the Club in maximising appropriate use of the stadium pitch while protecting playing quality and long-term surface performance.
  • Plan appropriate protection, preparation and reinstatement measures for non-football activity.
  • Assess weather and pitch conditions ahead of fixtures and events and advise relevant Club personnel on risks or required interventions.
  • Coordinate post-use recovery and maintenance activity to maximise surface recovery between fixtures and events.
  • Ensure goals, nets and other grounds-related football equipment are prepared, maintained and compliant with relevant requirements.
  • Liaise effectively with match officials, football authorities, visiting clubs, event organisers and other relevant parties on playing surface matters where required.

Pitch Infrastructure & Technology
  • Manage and monitor irrigation, drainage, undersoil heating and other pitch infrastructure.
  • Manage the effective deployment and maintenance of specialist turf equipment and technology.
  • Monitor the performance of pitch systems and identify maintenance, renewal or improvement requirements.
  • Ensure faults and performance issues are identified promptly and appropriate remedial action is taken.
  • Work with specialist contractors and consultants where required.

Team Leadership
  • Lead, manage and develop the Craven Cottage grounds team, comprising three direct reports.
  • Allocate duties, manage rotas and ensure appropriate staffing coverage across fixtures, events and operational requirements.
  • Set clear standards for performance, conduct and attendance.
  • Ensure team members are appropriately trained, qualified and competent for the work undertaken.
  • Conduct performance reviews and support continuing professional development.
  • Promote a positive, professional, accountable and collaborative team culture.
  • Ensure sufficient resilience exists within the team to maintain required standards during holidays, absence and periods of intensive stadium activity.

Equipment & Materials
  • Manage all grounds machinery, vehicles, tools and specialist equipment based at Craven Cottage.
  • Ensure equipment is appropriately stored, maintained, serviced and operated.
  • Maintain appropriate machinery replacement and lifecycle plans.
  • Manage the procurement, storage and control of fertilisers, pesticides, seed, materials and other grounds consumables.
  • Ensure appropriate stock levels are maintained while achieving value for money.
  • Ensure all chemicals and controlled materials are stored, used and disposed of safely and in accordance with applicable requirements.

Financial Management
  • Prepare, manage and monitor the Craven Cottage grounds operating budget.
  • Support annual CAPEX planning and prepare investment proposals for machinery, infrastructure and playing surface improvements.
  • Control departmental expenditure and ensure effective procurement and value for money.
  • Manage contractor expenditure and monitor performance against agreed scopes and budgets.
  • Provide appropriate financial and operational reporting.

Projects & Continuous Improvement
  • Lead closed-season pitch renovation and reconstruction works.
  • Develop proposals for pitch, machinery and infrastructure improvements.
  • Manage grounds-related projects from specification and procurement through to implementation.
  • Work effectively with specialist contractors, consultants and suppliers.
  • Maintain an up-to-date understanding of developments in sports turf management, agronomy, machinery and pitch technology.
  • Identify opportunities to improve playing surface quality, efficiency, sustainability and operational resilience.

Health, Safety & Compliance
  • Ensure safe systems of work are established and followed across all grounds operations.
  • Ensure appropriate risk assessments, method statements and operating procedures are in place.
  • Maintain a thorough working knowledge of relevant Health & Safety requirements associated with grounds operations.
  • Ensure the safe operation of machinery and vehicles and the safe use, storage and disposal of pesticides, fertilisers and other substances.
  • Ensure employees and contractors are appropriately trained, briefed and supervised.
  • Maintain appropriate departmental records relating to machinery, chemicals, maintenance, inspections and statutory requirements.
  • Respond appropriately to emergencies and report hazards, incidents or breaches promptly.

Communication & Collaboration

  • Maintain strong working relationships with Football Operations, Stadium Operations, Commercial, Events and other Club departments.
  • Communicate clearly regarding pitch condition, planned works, operational constraints and playing surface availability.
  • Provide clear professional advice on the suitability and timing of proposed pitch use, including football, commercial hires and events.
  • Work collaboratively with the Head of Grounds & Estates – Training Ground to share knowledge, resources and best practice where appropriate.
  • Maintain effective relationships with suppliers, contractors, consultants and football industry contacts.
  • Provide professional advice to the Chief Operating Officer and other senior management on playing surface matters, investment requirements and operational risks.

- Lead all aspects of preparation, maintenance and presentation of the Craven Cottage playing surface. - Ensure the pitch is maintained consistently to elite professional football standards. - Develop, implement and monitor annual and seasonal turf management programmes. - Plan and undertake mowing, aeration, fertilisation, irrigation, overseeding, topdressing, plant health and disease management programmes. - Monitor pitch condition and performance through appropriate testing, inspection and record keeping. - Monitor weather forecasts and ground conditions and adapt maintenance programmes accordingly. - Manage playing surface usage to protect pitch quality, recovery and long-term performance. - Maintain the highest standards of pitch presentation, including line marking, goal preparation and matchday set-up. - Plan and deliver annual and in-season renovation programmes.
Football, Pitch Use & Events
- Ensure the playing surface is fully prepared and presented for all First Team home fixtures. - Prepare and maintain the playing surface for approved Women’s and Academy fixtures and other football activity at Craven Cottage. - Work closely with Football Operations to understand fixture requirements and ensure appropriate preparation and recovery periods. - Work with Stadium Operations, Commercial and Events teams in planning pitch hires, events and other approved uses of the playing surface. - Assess proposed pitch activity and provide professional advice on its likely impact on surface condition, recovery and future football requirements. - Support the Club in maximising appropriate use of the stadium pitch while protecting playing quality and long-term surface performance. - Plan appropriate protection, preparation and reinstatement measures for non-football activity. - Assess weather and pitch conditions ahead of fixtures and events and advise relevant Club personnel on risks or required interventions. - Coordinate post-use recovery and maintenance activity to maximise surface recovery between fixtures and events. - Ensure goals, nets and other grounds-related football equipment are prepared, maintained and compliant with relevant requirements. - Liaise effectively with match officials, football authorities, visiting clubs, event organisers and other relevant parties on playing surface matters where required.
Pitch Infrastructure & Technology
- Manage and monitor irrigation, drainage, undersoil heating and other pitch infrastructure. - Manage the effective deployment and maintenance of specialist turf equipment and technology. - Monitor the performance of pitch systems and identify maintenance, renewal or improvement requirements. - Ensure faults and performance issues are identified promptly and appropriate remedial action is taken. - Work with specialist contractors and consultants where required.
Team Leadership
- Lead, manage and develop the Craven Cottage grounds team, comprising three direct reports. - Allocate duties, manage rotas and ensure appropriate staffing coverage across fixtures, events and operational requirements. - Set clear standards for performance, conduct and attendance. - Ensure team members are appropriately trained, qualified and competent for the work undertaken. - Conduct performance reviews and support continuing professional development. - Promote a positive, professional, accountable and collaborative team culture. - Ensure sufficient resilience exists within the team to maintain required standards during holidays, absence and periods of intensive stadium activity.
Equipment & Materials
- Manage all grounds machinery, vehicles, tools and specialist equipment based at Craven Cottage. - Ensure equipment is appropriately stored, maintained, serviced and operated. - Maintain appropriate machinery replacement and lifecycle plans. - Manage the procurement, storage and control of fertilisers, pesticides, seed, materials and other grounds consumables. - Ensure appropriate stock levels are maintained while achieving value for money. - Ensure all chemicals and controlled materials are stored, used and disposed of safely and in accordance with applicable requirements.
Financial Management
- Prepare, manage and monitor the Craven Cottage grounds operating budget. - Support annual CAPEX planning and prepare investment proposals for machinery, infrastructure and playing surface improvements. - Control departmental expenditure and ensure effective procurement and value for money. - Manage contractor expenditure and monitor performance against agreed scopes and budgets. - Provide appropriate financial and operational reporting.
Projects & Continuous Improvement
- Lead closed-season pitch renovation and reconstruction works. - Develop proposals for pitch, machinery and infrastructure improvements. - Manage grounds-related projects from specification and procurement through to implementation. - Work effectively with specialist contractors, consultants and suppliers. - Maintain an up-to-date understanding of developments in sports turf management, agronomy, machinery and pitch technology. - Identify opportunities to improve playing surface quality, efficiency, sustainability and operational resilience.
Health, Safety & Compliance
- Ensure safe systems of work are established and followed across all grounds operations. - Ensure appropriate risk assessments, method statements and operating procedures are in place. - Maintain a thorough working knowledge of relevant Health & Safety requirements associated with grounds operations. - Ensure the safe operation of machinery and vehicles and the safe use, storage and disposal of pesticides, fertilisers and other substances. - Ensure employees and contractors are appropriately trained, briefed and supervised. - Maintain appropriate departmental records relating to machinery, chemicals, maintenance, inspections and statutory requirements. - Respond appropriately to emergencies and report hazards, incidents or breaches promptly.
Communication & Collaboration
- Maintain strong working relationships with Football Operations, Stadium Operations, Commercial, Events and other Club departments. - Communicate clearly regarding pitch condition, planned works, operational constraints and playing surface availability. - Provide clear professional advice on the suitability and timing of proposed pitch use, including football, commercial hires and events. - Work collaboratively with the Head of Grounds & Estates – Training Ground to share knowledge, resources and best practice where appropriate. - Maintain effective relationships with suppliers, contractors, consultants and football industry contacts. - Provide professional advice to the Chief Operating Officer and other senior management on playing surface matters, investment requirements and operational risks.

job.title: Chef De Partie
job.html_description:
Position Purpose 
 

  • We are looking for a chef with a background in catering for professional sports teams to join our passionate nutrition focused team.

  • You will support our Head Chef and Sous Chef in providing balanced, nutritional and high quality meals to our players and support staff at the training ground.

  • A good basis of nutrition helps our players to achieve their individual nutritional goals, ultimately enhancing health, recovery and performance.

  • To lead the kitchen team in preparing and providing meals to our youth and women teams.

  • Some travel with teams to away games may be necessary, following their weekly schedule/fixtures, ensuring all food provided to them meets the presentation, taste and performance need of the group.

Requirements

Requirements and Responsibilities
 

  • Work with the Head Chef and independently to create and develop exciting seasonal menus. 

  • Prepare meals for youth and women teams working within the nutritional guidelines and ensure junior team members are working correctly to achieve this with you.

  • Instruct junior team members accordingly to ensure youth and women teams' meals are delivered on time and presented to a high standard.

  • Support and lead junior members of the kitchen team.

  • Check stock requirements and order accordingly in the Head/Sous chef absence.

  • Travel with teams in the UK and abroad when required as the catering team representative and provide food provisions as requested.

  • Assist in the preparation of all travel food requirements whilst displaying good organisational skills.

  • Support Head/Sous chef to deliver constantly high quality food in a timely manner.

  • Cover Sous chefs' role as and when required.

  • Working closely with the Supervisor to ensure the highest level of food safety and hygiene are maintained. Compliance with COSHH.

  • Flexibility to work around the teams schedules.



Essential and Desirable
 

The Chef De Partie must have: 

  • Minimum of 1 year experience providing food to sports teams/athletes
  • Level 2 NVQ Professional Cookery or equivalent
  • Excellent communication skill to lead the junior kitchen team
  • Works well under pressure with the ability to remain calm with last minute schedule changes
 
Ideally, the Chef De Partie will: 
  • Football specific experience
  • Level 2 Food Hygiene certificate
  • Performance nutrition knowledge

job.title: Casual Academy Scout (Midlands)
job.html_description:
The National Academy scouting team is responsible for identifying and monitoring players either from grassroots or other Academies in national regions. They will complete reports on players and share information with other Academy staff to develop a range of player intelligence across the local area. 

There is a particular interest for us to recruit within the following teams: 
- Grassroots – Midlands 
- Academy- Midlands

Responsibilities

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role:
• To manage your individual weekend schedule and regularly attend fixtures within your region or
across your phase.
• To complete reports on players all players with potential across your region and phase.
• Network with other national scouts to share information on potential target players.
• To keep National and department Managers informed of high potential players across their area or
age phase.
• To support with the ongoing communication to the families of players within our TID programmes
and on trial as and when required.
• To support the delivery of Talent ID programmes and events as and when required.
• Participate in scouting team meetings to further discuss succession planning and their identified
target players.
• To attend department meetings and participate in all CPD and required safeguarding training when
appropriate.

Requirements

The Casual Academy Scout (Midlands) must have:
• Knowledge and networks within the local area they scout.
• Previous experience scouting for another Academy (Cat 1, 2 or 3)
• FA Talent ID Level 2
• FA Safeguarding

Ideally, the Casual Academy Scout (Midlands) will:
• Previous experience scouting for another Cat 1 Academy.
• FA Level 2 Coaching
• Full Driver’s License

job.title: Mental Health Worker (Casual Matchday Role)
job.html_description:
Join Fulham Football Club's matchday wellbeing team and help create a safe, supportive environment for supporters and visitors. This is a unique opportunity to use your mental health experience in one of football's most iconic settings.

Responsibilities

Applications close on 19th August.

Requirements

What you'll do
  • Provide compassionate, non-clinical emotional support on matchdays.
  • Offer active listening, reassurance and signposting to appropriate services.
  • Be a calm, approachable presence in our designated wellbeing spaces.
  • Respond to safeguarding and suicide risk concerns using agreed procedures.
  • Attend pre-match briefings, post-match debriefs and complete basic reporting.

What we're looking for
  • Mental health training and/or relevant qualifications.
  • Experience supporting people experiencing emotional distress.
  • Excellent communication and active listening skills.
  • A calm, professional approach under pressure.
  • A strong understanding of safeguarding, confidentiality and professional boundaries.

The role
  • Casual matchday position based at Craven Cottage.
  • Regular availability for home fixtures preferred, opportunities for job sharing considered.
  • Attendance at ad hoc events, where available.

If you're passionate about mental health and want to help make every matchday a positive experience, we'd love to hear from you.
